title: Meridian Systems - migration discovery (hosted -> private)
next_steps: Send SOC 2 + ISO docs and KMS integration notes
Share sample benchmarking spreadsheet and test vectors
Schedule technical deep dive with infra team (Jared + Marcus) next week
Provision trial Dedicated capacity for 2-week pilot
action_items: Samira: Send security packet and pricing sheet by 2026-12-20
Jared: Draft benchmark config and propose three workloads by 2026-12-22
Marcus: Provide sample prompts and peak QPS estimates by 2026-12-21
summary: Initial migration discovery for Meridian Systems evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency-sensitive customer-facing assistants. Key concerns: data residency, KMS/HSM integration, latency parity with current vLLM/TGI stack, and cost sensitivity during pilot.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Samira from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Jared who is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lena Ortiz: Good, thanks. We appreciate you fitting us in, I know year-end is busy.
[00:12] Jared Coleman: Hi Lena, Marcus, Priya, Diego — excited to dig in. Quick agenda: understand your current infra + constraints, success criteria for migration, and outline next steps for a pilot.
[00:25] Marcus Chen: Great, I'll kick off with our setup — we run a vLLM + TGI based stack in our data centers, some elastic GKE clusters for user-facing inference. We optimized kernels ourselves; latency's pretty tight, 80 to 120ms p95 for the short prompt flows.
[00:40] Diego Alvarez: Yeah and for heavier sequences we see spikes, but we use prefix KV caching and some request coalescing. We also have an Azure-hosted failover for peak hours.
[00:52] Priya Rao: From security: we need enterprise controls — KMS integration (we use HashiCorp and Azure Key Vault), audit logs, SSO with Okta, RBAC. Data residency is a requirement for EU customers. We're SOC 2 in progress.
[01:06] Samira Patel: Thanks, that's super helpful. Just to confirm — are you actively evaluating a move off the self-hosted vLLM/TGI stack to a hosted provider or considering dedicated/private Redwood deployments?
[01:18] Lena Ortiz: All of the above. We want options: hopefully we can get parity on quality and latency with Redwood Dedicated or Private. Hosted might be easier but we have data residency and KMS requirements so Private or Dedicated sounds likely.
[01:31] Jared Coleman: Understood. On parity — we do a model compatibility pass and an eval sprint. For vLLM/TGI models we typically map to equivalent model variants in our catalog; sometimes kernel/quantization differences change token timing but we can run head-to-head bench.
[01:45] Marcus Chen: Two immediate questions: 1) how do you handle KV cache and warm starts? 2) what's the round-trip to a private VPC host — network overhead?
[01:56] Jared Coleman: Good Qs. KV cache: our runtime supports session-level KV caches and automatic prefix caching — you can persist per-customer caches if you run Private or Dedicated. For warm starts we support fast restore paths that mimic vLLM behavior, though exact performance depends on quantization.
[02:14] Samira Patel: For network, if you pick Private in your VPC or on-prem package, we don't traverse public internet for request-to-model traffic — that's inside your network. If you look at Dedicated (hosted in our cloud), we provide private peering and regional endpoints to cut latency.
[02:32] Lena Ortiz: Okay that helps. Another concern: we use custom instruction tuning and a few minor model patches — will those translate or do we need to retrain?
[02:44] Jared Coleman: If you have instruction-tuned weights, we can host compatibles; for tokenization and special tokens we do a quick ingest check. Often it's a config mapping not a full retrain. We'll check parity with your eval prompts.
[02:58] Priya Rao: On encryption, do you support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed KMS? We can't expose plaintext model keys.
[03:06] Jared Coleman: Yes — Private supports CMKs and HSM integrations; Dedicated has KMS integrations and we can support bring-your-own-key workflows. We'll share our KMS integration doc.
[03:17] Diego Alvarez: How about tooling — can we get logs at the token level? I need to map latency to internal traces.
[03:23] Samira Patel: Redwood Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns and tracing hooks. For Private, those hooks can be sent to your internal tracing endpoints.
[03:33] Marcus Chen: Great. Pricing model: you're usage-based for hosted, reserved for Dedicated — but for a pilot what's typical?
[03:40] Samira Patel: We usually offer a short trial: a two-week Dedicated trial for capacity and a small Private eval for teams doing on-prem — costs are capped in pilot. We'll draft pricing scenarios based on your QPS and target latency.
[03:52] Lena Ortiz: For QPS, our peak is about 120 RPS across all regions, typical inference size ~120 tokens. We're very sensitive to per-token cost because of volume.
[04:04] Jared Coleman: Noted. We'll run cost models for three profiles: conservative batch, low latency optimized, and a hybrid with prefix caching.
[04:12] Samira Patel: Can I ask about stakeholders and timeline? Who signs off and what's the target?
[04:18] Lena Ortiz: I'm the exec sponsor, Marcus is the technical owner, Priya signs off on security, procurement will be involved for contracts. Timeline: pilot in January, decision by end of Q1.
[04:29] Priya Rao: Also need to check regulatory constraints for EU and UK customers — data at rest and in transit, plus audit logging retention.
[04:38] Samira Patel: We can map our compliance docs and retention options. For audit logs, Private can keep retention on your side; Dedicated offers configurable retention windows.
[04:47] Diego Alvarez: A bit of friction we ran into when migrating from Anthropic — the model outputs shifted slightly due to tokenization differences, and we had to tweak prompts. How do you measure eval parity?
[04:59] Jared Coleman: We do an eval parity sprint — you give us production prompts and expected outputs, we run the same prompts across your current stack and our variants, and we annotate differences. We'll also run automated ROUGE/BLEU style scoring and human checks for business-critical flows.
[05:14] Lena Ortiz: That sounds right. How long does that typically take?
[05:18] Jared Coleman: For a focused set of 500–2,000 prompts, about a week to collect results and a short report. If you want human review, add another week.
[05:29] Marcus Chen: Network peering — you mentioned private peering for Dedicated; is that via AWS Direct Connect/ExpressRoute or a more generic setup?
[05:38] Samira Patel: We use cloud provider peering partners when helpful. For Dedicated we can set up private networking that looks like Direct Connect, or you can run Private in your VPC if you want full control.
[05:49] Priya Rao: Can we get a list of certifications and third-party assessments?
[05:52] Samira Patel: Absolutely — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 summary, and our pen test report redacted. We'll include that in the packet.
[06:00] Diego Alvarez: Operational question: how are rollouts handled? Canary, A/B, automatic fallback?
[06:05] Jared Coleman: Redwood supports canary and A/B policy rollouts, plus automated fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained. For Dedicated you can pin versions.
[06:16] Marcus Chen: Okay, concrete ask — can you provision a Dedicated trial where we can run our 120 RPS benchmark and test latency with our prompt set?
[06:24] Samira Patel: Yes, that's the typical next step. We'll need your prompt set and a small benchmark config — Jared will own drafting that.
[06:31] Jared Coleman: I'll propose three workload configs: short-chat, multi-turn assistant, and long-form generation. We'll tune batching and sequence lengths to match your traffic.
[06:41] Lena Ortiz: Any gotchas re: quantization? We use 4-bit quant in vLLM to save memory.
[06:47] Jared Coleman: Our runtime supports quantized paths; sometimes 4-bit leads to minor quality changes. We'll surface delta metrics in the parity report and suggest quant profiles per model.
[06:58] Priya Rao: What about legal terms for Private/on-prem — can we get a data processing addendum and custom SLAs?
[07:05] Samira Patel: Yes, onboarding enterprise privacy contracts is standard; we can add DPAs and custom SLA clauses for Dedicated/Private.
[07:13] Marcus Chen: Alright, for the benchmarking, do you need us to run any local agents or can Redwood drive all the tests remotely?
[07:20] Jared Coleman: We can drive tests from our side if you provide secure access to the endpoints or we can provide a small test harness you run internally. For Private, it's often easier to run internally with our config.
[07:33] Diego Alvarez: One more — provider lock-in concerns. If we decide to leave down the line, how easy is it to export logs, cached embeddings, and move back to our vLLM/TGI setup?
[07:44] Samira Patel: We provide export tooling for logs and embeddings, and you can snapshot model configs. For Private/on-prem you keep data custody so exit is straightforward; for Dedicated we have export APIs and will work with you on migration plans.
[07:58] Lena Ortiz: This is helpful. I think the next concrete things for us: get the security docs, pricing, and the benchmark plan.
[08:06] Samira Patel: Agreed. I'll send the security packet and an initial pricing sketch. Jared will send the benchmark config and we'll set up the Dedicated trial.
[08:14] Priya Rao: Can we loop in procurement and legal on the next call?
[08:18] Samira Patel: Yes — let's propose a follow-up next Thursday and invite procurement.
[08:22] Marcus Chen: Sounds good. One note — for EU traffic we may need regionally isolated model endpoints; what are options?
[08:29] Jared Coleman: We can run Dedicated in EU regions or deploy Private in your EU VPC. For hosted we can pin to EU-only endpoints as well. We'll capture that in the packet.
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: Cool, thanks everyone. Anything else?
[08:44] Diego Alvarez: Not from me.
[08:46] Priya Rao: No.
[08:47] Samira Patel: Great. Recap: security docs + pricing (Samira), benchmark configs + pilot provisioning (Jared), sample prompts and QPS (Marcus). We'll target the follow-up the week of 2026-12-22.
[08:59] Jared Coleman: I'll drop the benchmark spreadsheet and a proposed runbook. Expect the invite.
[09:04] Samira Patel: Thanks all, talk soon.
[09:06] Lena Ortiz: Thanks. Bye.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings: 'Direct Connect' sometimes transcribed as 'direct connectable', 'vLLM' sometimes 'V L L M' in audio. Speakers sometimes overlap; timestamps are approximate.
